title: Dependra Architecture Manifest
description: The Dependra landscape manifest: the versioned contract a repo (or an AI agent, or your own tooling) emits to describe its architecture. Producers emit this shape; consumers — the GitHub Action, the validation CLI, and the Dependra ingest API — map it onto your Dependra landscape. Enum casing is significant: use the exact values listed. `description` is a short inline one/two-line summary (string only); the long-form README home is `documentation`, which also accepts a { file: <path.md> } reference. Unknown/forward fields are tolerated (ignored), never rejected.

id.description: Stable id / technicalName. Lowercase, must start alphanumeric, allows dots/dashes/underscores. Unique within its collection in the merged manifest.

technicalName.description: Explicit technicalName. When present it wins over id (the golden manifest sets both to the same value). Same lowercase/alphanumeric-start rules.

description.description: A short, single-/two-line inline SUMMARY (string only). A {file:...} reference is NOT valid here — that belongs on `documentation`. Kept small by design: the long-form README home is `documentation`.

documentation.description: The README / long-form home for this entity: either an inline Markdown string, or a { file: <path.md> } reference. A file reference is resolved by the CLI/Action into this entity's documentation before ingest.

file.description: Path to a Markdown file whose contents become this entity's documentation.

lifecycleState.description: Lifecycle state of the application. One of the listed values (exact casing).

criticalityTier.description: Criticality tier: how much business impact when this application is unavailable.
enumDescriptions: Failure disrupts day-to-day operations but workarounds exist.
Failure significantly impacts core business operations.
Total failure causes immediate, severe impact across the organization.

dataClassification.description: Data classification of the data this application handles.

sourcing.description: Where the code came from: developed (in-house), openSource, contracted (built to order by an external party), or vendored (licensed/subscribed product). Orthogonal to modificationLevel.
enumDescriptions: Externally sourced code — typically open source — that we run and maintain ourselves.
Built to order for us by an external party.
Licensed or subscribed as a product from a supplier.

modificationLevel.description: How much the code has been changed since it was sourced: offTheShelf (used as shipped), configured (supported configuration only), customized (altered beyond supported configuration), or forked (source diverged from upstream). Orthogonal to sourcing.
enumDescriptions: Extended or altered beyond supported configuration.
Source diverged from upstream and maintained separately.

vendor.description: Vendor display name (e.g. 'Salesforce', 'Microsoft'). Resolve-or-create by name (case-insensitive, per tenant) against the vendor registry — unlike technicalName references elsewhere in the manifest, this is a plain display name.

environment.description: Deployment environment label (free-text, e.g. production, staging).

tags.description: Free-text tags for grouping and filtering.

team.description: Optional id of the owning team. Forward field — currently ignored by ingest, reserved for team linkage.

productSuite.description: Optional id of the owning product suite. Forward field — currently ignored by ingest, reserved for product-suite linkage.

notes.description: Free-text operator notes. Forward field — currently ignored by ingest.

items.description: An application: a logical product/system that owns one or more components. Declaring it here masters it in Dependra.

applications.description: Applications you master in this repo. Each declared application becomes an authoritative (mastered) entity in Dependra.

id.description: Stable id / technicalName. Lowercase, must start alphanumeric, allows dots/dashes/underscores. Unique within its collection in the merged manifest.

technicalName.description: Explicit technicalName. When present it wins over id. Same lowercase/alphanumeric-start rules.

application.description: Id of the owning application in this manifest.

description.description: A short, single-/two-line inline SUMMARY (string only). A {file:...} reference is NOT valid here — that belongs on `documentation`. Kept small by design: the long-form README home is `documentation`.

documentation.description: The README / long-form home for this entity: either an inline Markdown string, or a { file: <path.md> } reference. A file reference is resolved by the CLI/Action into this entity's documentation before ingest.

file.description: Path to a Markdown file whose contents become this entity's documentation.

kind.description: Component kind: what sort of runtime unit this is.
enumDescriptions: An event bus / streaming platform (e.g. Kafka).
An integration / connector to an external system.
Anything that doesn't fit the other kinds.

runtime.description: Runtime type: how/where this component runs.

networkExposure.description: Network exposure: how reachable this component is from outside.
enumDescriptions: Cannot be reached from the Internet. Reachable only from other zones with connectivity.
Accepts internet traffic via the zone's infrastructure components (firewalls, gateways, proxies). No explicit dependency edges needed — the path is inferred from zone connectivity.
Has its own external IP addresses and bypasses any zone-defined infrastructure nodes.

egressMode.description: Egress mode: how this component reaches out to the network.

protectionMechanisms.description: Security protection mechanisms at this component's network boundary — either protecting it (in front of it) OR provided by this component when it is itself a proxy/gateway/WAF. Common values: WAF, RateLimiting, mTLS, ApiKey, IpAllowlist, DDoSProtection, GeoRestriction, BotProtection, TLSTermination (terminates inbound TLS), TLSReencryption (terminates then re-encrypts to the origin — 'full SSL'), mTLSToOrigin (presents a client cert to the origin).

statusPageUrl.description: Public status/health page URL for this component, if any.

name.description: Endpoint name, unique within the component (e.g. "public-api", "admin", "grpc").

protocol.description: Protocol exposed (e.g. HTTPS, gRPC, AMQP, PostgreSQL).

port.description: Port the endpoint listens on, if fixed.

transportEncryption.description: Minimum transport encryption the endpoint enforces (e.g. "TLS1.3", "mTLS", "None").

authProvider.description: Optional id of an identity component that provides this auth (e.g. your hosted IdP).

items.description: An authentication method an endpoint accepts.

A network endpoint a component exposes. Its declared posture (protocol, port, transport encryption, accepted auth methods) is the exposed attack surface — captured independently of whether any dependency consumes it.

endpoints.description: Network endpoints this component EXPOSES — its attack surface. An endpoint is inventoried whether or not any dependency consumes it, so its declared security posture (transport encryption, accepted auth methods) is captured independently of who connects.

technology.description: Id of the technology (declared in top-level `technologies:` or known to the tenant).

current.description: Whether this is the component's current version of the technology. Defaults to true.

items.description: Links a component to a technology it uses, at a specific version.

technologies.description: Technologies this component uses, with the per-component version. The same shared technology (e.g. .NET) can appear on many components at different versions — multi-targeting is normal. Reference a technology declared in the top-level `technologies:` block (or already known to the tenant).

isExternal.description: True if this component is external / third-party (not built in-house).

dataClassification.description: Data classification of the data this component handles.

gitRepoUrl.description: URL of the git repository backing this component.

gitTag.description: Git tag / release this manifest snapshot corresponds to.

gitCommitSha.description: Git commit SHA this manifest snapshot corresponds to. Forward field — currently ignored by ingest.

tags.description: Free-text tags for grouping and filtering.

items.description: A component: a deployable/runtime unit (API, database, queue, worker, …) owned by an application. Declaring it here masters it in Dependra.

components.description: Components (deployable/runtime units) you master in this repo. Each declared component becomes an authoritative (mastered) entity, owned by its application.

from.description: Source component id: the component that depends on the target.

to.description: Target component id: the component being depended upon.

type.description: Dependency type: the nature of the interaction (Calls/Reads/Writes/Publishes/Consumes/…).
enumDescriptions: Publishes messages/events to the target (e.g. a topic/queue).
Network traffic flow to the target (e.g. through a gateway/proxy).
Uses the target as an identity provider (authentication).
Both reads and writes the target (e.g. a primary datastore).
Publish/subscribe relationship with the target broker/channel.

mode.description: Dependency mode: how tightly coupled the source is to the target's availability.
enumDescriptions: Hard dependency: the source cannot function without the target.
Soft dependency: the source degrades but keeps working without the target.
Asynchronous: the source is decoupled in time (queued/eventual).
Degraded: the source runs in a reduced mode without the target.

required.description: Whether the source hard-requires the target. Defaults to true.

propagates.description: Whether failure of the target propagates to the source in blast-radius. Defaults to true.

description.description: A short, single-/two-line inline SUMMARY (string only). A {file:...} reference is NOT valid here — that belongs on `documentation`. Kept small by design: the long-form README home is `documentation`.

protocol.description: Communication protocol (free-text, e.g. HTTPS, gRPC, AMQP). Security register.

transportEncryption.description: Transport encryption method (free-text, e.g. TLS 1.3, mTLS, none). Security register.

endpointAuthMethod.description: Endpoint authentication method (free-text, e.g. OAuth2, API key, mTLS). Security register.

targetEndpoint.description: Name of the specific endpoint on the TARGET component this edge connects to (must match one of that component's declared endpoints). Binds the edge to that exposed endpoint's auth register — pair with endpointAuthMethod.

channelType.description: Messaging channel type for pub/sub & queue dependencies.
enumDescriptions: A pub/sub topic (fan-out to many subscribers).

broker.description: Id of the broker component for pub/sub dependencies.

timeoutMs.description: Optional timeout for this call, in milliseconds (>= 0).

evidence.description: How this dependency was established. Defaults to Declared.
enumDescriptions: Declared by hand / by an author.

dataClass.description: Data classification carried over this dependency. Part of the data-in-transit security register. Forward field — currently ignored by ingest.

endpoint.description: Endpoint reference (URL/path) for this dependency. Part of the data-in-transit security register. Forward field — currently ignored by ingest.

source.description: How this edge was produced: 'authored' for hand-/agent-written manifests, 'ci-derived' for edges inferred by automated code analysis. Defaults to authored. Forward field — currently ignored by ingest.

confidence.description: Optional confidence score (0..1) for machine-derived edges. Forward field — currently ignored by ingest.

dataset.description: Dataset id (a declared dataset's id) that flows over this edge.

sourceRole.description: Role of the SOURCE component (the edge's `from`) with respect to this dataset: Producer/Consumer/Processor/Store. A Producer→Consumer pairing is what makes lineage show FLOW direction. Defaults to Consumer.

targetRole.description: Role of the TARGET component (the edge's `to`) with respect to this dataset: Producer/Consumer/Processor/Store. Defaults to Consumer.

sourceIsSourceOfTruth.description: Whether the SOURCE component is the system of record (source of truth) for this dataset on this edge.

targetIsSourceOfTruth.description: Whether the TARGET component is the system of record (source of truth) for this dataset on this edge.

items.description: A dataset that flows across one dependency edge (data lineage). Identify the dataset by id; the edge is the parent dependency's from/to/type.

datasets.description: Datasets that FLOW across this edge — the data lineage. Each entry names a dataset and the role of the SOURCE and TARGET components with respect to it (Producer/Consumer/Processor/Store). This is what turns a lineage diagram from 'which components touch the dataset' into a directional flow 'producer → dataset → consumer'. Prefer this over only listing a dataset's components: the edge is where the flow lives.

items.description: A dependency edge: the source component (from) depends on the target component (to). Directional; drives blast-radius propagation and the data-in-transit security register.

dependencies.description: Dependency edges between components: who calls/reads/writes/publishes to whom. Drives blast-radius and the data-in-transit security register.

category.description: Radar category: which quadrant this technology sits in.

items.description: A technology in use across the estate — a FACT (identity + category). Radar governance (recommendation, EOL target) is set by EA/CIO in Dependra and is not declarable in a manifest.

technologies.description: Technologies (languages, frameworks, platforms, tools) used across the estate — identity + category ONLY. This declares the FACT that a technology exists and is used; per-component versions live on each component's `technologies` links. Radar GOVERNANCE (adopt/hold/retire recommendations, EOL target dates) is an EA/CIO decision made in Dependra and is NOT declarable here.

segments.description: Ids of segments this actor belongs to.

items.description: A segment: an audience grouping that actors belong to (e.g. Retail, Enterprise).

segments.description: Segments: audience groupings an actor belongs to.

items.description: An application: a logical product/system that owns one or more components. Declaring it here masters it in Dependra.

applications.description: Applications this repo references but does not own. Stub semantics; provide only id + name.

items.description: A component: a deployable/runtime unit (API, database, queue, worker, …) owned by an application. Declaring it here masters it in Dependra.

components.description: Components this repo references but does not own. Stub semantics; provide only id + name + application.

stubs.description: Applications and components this repo REFERENCES but does NOT own/master (e.g. a service defined in another repo). Everything here is a STUB: created if absent, left untouched if it already exists (never reconciled or deleted), and promoted to mastered when the repo that owns it later declares it under the top-level applications:/components:. Keep stubs minimal — id + name (+ application for a component).
